newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols remain at depressed levels.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols remain at depressed levels.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. interest rate options stuck at very low levels Monday as the underlying futures traded within the previous session's ranges.
Analysts said the subdued volatility reflects traders' complacent attitude toward the market's downward price trend.
"It suggests the market is comfortable with the current trend," said one bond options analyst. "You have to have a good reason to fight a seven-month low."
On Friday, June bond futures slid to their lowest level since September.

Implied volatility for May Treasury bond options was quoted at 7.35 percent late in today's session, down slightly from 7.40 at the opening and after shedding a full point on Friday on the heels of neutral U.S. employment report. for March. June was unchanged from opening levels at 8.50 percent.

Volatilities were also down substantially for Eurodollar options, bolstering conventional wisdom that the Federal Reserve will have to raise short-term rates by another 25 to 50 basis points in the next five to six months to cool the economy, said John Nyhoff, chief economist for Tokyo-Mitsubishi Futures (U.S.A.) Inc.

June was quoted late in the session at 7.0 percent, unchanged from late Friday, with September down 0.3 to 10.2, December steady at 12.0 and March also steady at 13.3. June 1998 was at 14.3 percent and September 1998 at 15.5, both also unchanged from Friday.
Volatility "cone" analysis for front-month September options shows volatility at unprecented lows for this stage in the options' life cycle, Nyhoff said.
While 10.0 percent could be expected to hold as support, he cautioned it was difficult to predict a floor with volatility in uncharted territory at these levels.

Volatilities for short-dated mid-curve options, those that expire in 1997 but are priced from 1998 futures, were unchanged at 15.0 percent in June and 15.3 in September, also exceptionally low levels, analysts said.

However, floor traders in both Treasury bond and Eurodollar options said they expected volatilities to bounce back somewhat before Friday, when March producer price and retail sales data are due for release.
June bond volatility should be able to climb back above 9.0 percent, the bond options analyst said.

If retail sales and PPI, along with the following Tuesday's consumer price data, fail to indicate inflation is accelerating, look for volatility rates to come off again after those reports, traders said.
